blocks.label: Important distinction
blocks.text: A flight dispatcher and an air traffic controller perform different jobs. A flight dispatcher supports an airline's flight planning, operational monitoring and dispatch decisions, while an air traffic controller manages aircraft movements within assigned airspace or at an airport. The exact qualification and authorization required for flight dispatch depend on the country and the employer.

A Flight Dispatcher helps an airline plan and monitor flights safely and efficiently. The role involves analyzing weather, flight routes, aircraft performance, fuel requirements, airport conditions, operational restrictions and other factors that may affect a flight.

In airline operations, flight dispatchers coordinate with pilots, operations control teams, meteorological services, airport personnel and other aviation professionals. In jurisdictions where licensed dispatchers share operational control with the pilot-in-command, the dispatcher also has defined legal responsibilities.

items.text: Prepare and review operational flight plans.
Analyze weather forecasts, observations and aviation warnings.
Review NOTAMs and airport operating conditions.
Calculate or verify fuel requirements and operational reserves.
Evaluate route options, alternate airports and flight restrictions.
Review aircraft performance and payload-related operational limits.
Coordinate with pilots and airline operations control.
Monitor flights and assess changing weather or operational conditions.
Support rerouting, delay, diversion and disruption decisions.
Maintain accurate flight documentation and operational records.
Follow airline procedures, safety management systems and applicable aviation regulations.

For an India-based career, focus on the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), applicable Civil Aviation Requirements, Aircraft Rules and the airline's approved operations manuals.

In India, flight dispatchers require the applicable DGCA approval before being assigned regulated duties. The specific qualification and training requirements should be checked against the latest applicable DGCA requirements and the prospective airline's procedures.

blocks.text: All training exercises should use approved procedures and instructor-supervised simulations—not live operational decision-making.

The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) publishes competency-based guidance for flight operations officers and flight dispatchers. Its training resources include operational flight planning and flight-follow-up training.

A university degree in aviation or air navigation can provide a useful foundation, but a degree alone does not automatically qualify a graduate to perform flight dispatcher duties. Approved training, assessments, authorization and operator-specific requirements may also apply.

1. Flight Dispatch Prepare operational flight plans and coordinate required dispatch processes.
2. Flight Following Monitor flights and provide relevant operational information and assistance to flight crews.
3. Airline Operations Control Coordinate flight schedules, aircraft availability, delays, diversions and disruptions.
4. Flight Planning Focus on routing, fuel planning, navigation information and operational documentation.
5. Aviation Safety Support safety reporting, operational risk assessment and safety management processes.
6. Operations Performance Analysis Analyze delays, fuel-related indicators, operational efficiency and disruption patterns.
